subject: Headroom drain: CTO authorization + customer commitment plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Headroom drain: CTO authorization + customer commitment plan

Team — quick high-priority summary: ClearBridge (priority account) is showing sustained QPS above their reserved commitment for the last 90 minutes and we're seeing 95th/99th latency spikes and an uptick in 5xx errors. Attached snapshot (cb_metrics_qps.csv) shows the tail.

Immediate asks:
- Can infra/ops confirm whether this is single-pool saturation vs cross-tenant interference? (David / Marcus)
- Please list the minimum exec authorization needed to temporarily increase dedicated headroom or enable a short-term burst pool. I need a concrete approval request I can take to Lauren/CTO.
- Product & SRE: suggested mitigation steps and estimated time-to-impact (evict idle sessions, lighter model variant fallback, caching adjustments).

Customer is already looped in (they reported increased latency). We should be explicit on a mitigation ETA and whether we will offer a credit. I want to propose: authorize a 4-hour burst of dedicated capacity + 20% service credit for May, conditioned on a postmortem and performance tuning plan. Please respond with actions + owners within the hour.

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
[attachment: cb_metrics_qps.csv]

From: David Kim <david@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Headroom drain: CTO authorization + customer commitment plan

Vivek — quick technical readout (short):
- Observed: dedicated-pool-42 is saturated. Long-running sessions (avg seq len ~2.4x baseline) holding KV caches; continuous batching starving latency-sensitive requests.
- Root signals: sudden increase in one tenant's streaming scoring jobs (appears to be a misrouted batch), KV cache miss rate jumped; model variant fallback attempted but some requests were pinned to a high-memory variant causing OOM thrashing on 2 nodes.

Immediate mitigations (can do in ~15–45m):
1) Evict idle/old sessions for tenant (risk: small number of in-flight operations) — OWNER: Marcus — ETA 15m.
2) Enable lightweight quantized fallback model for real-time routes (lowers memory/latency) — OWNER: Product Ops (David) — ETA 20m to roll to canary, 45m to rollout if green.
3) Apply prefix caching policy for the tenant's frequent prefixes — OWNER: SRE (Naomi) — ETA 30m to test.
4) Request infra to authorize short burst (temp +10 GPUs) to Dedicated pools for 4 hours — REQ: exec/CTO approval.

I attached the canary heap dump and tail traces (canary_heapdump.txt) to help infra triage memory/OOM edges. If we get exec approval for the burst now, we can avoid failed requests and reduce customer impact while we implement the config changes.

--
David
David Kim
VP, Reliability Engineering
[attachment: canary_heapdump.txt]

From: Elena Rossi <elena@clearbridge.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david@redwood.ai>, ClearBridge Ops <ops@clearbridge.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Headroom drain: CTO authorization + customer commitment plan

Vivek — thanks for the quick flag.

Short version from our side: an internal data team accidentally kicked off a larger-than-intended scoring run against the production endpoint (it should have gone to a staging key). That job ramped QPS and kept many long-lived streaming sessions open; we only noticed after the latency rose. We are pausing that job immediately.

We appreciate the mitigation suggestions. From ClearBridge's perspective we need:
- Immediate reduction in errors / latency so customer-facing users are not impacted (status updates every 30 minutes until resolved).
- Confirmation on whether you can keep the production endpoint stable for the next 24 hours while we audit and add safeguards.
- Clarity on what remediation/redress (credits) we can expect under our SLA.

We are ready to coordinate - point us to the status channel and we will provide logs for the misrouted run.

Elena Rossi
Head of ML Ops, ClearBridge
elena@clearbridge.com

To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Headroom drain: CTO authorization + customer commitment plan — Exec ask

Lauren — looping you for CTO authorization. Summary + ask:
- Issue: ClearBridge produced unintended high-QPS workload causing dedicated pool saturation; tail latency and 5xxs increased. Technical mitigations ready (evict sessions, quantized fallback, caching) — ops estimates 15–45m to materially reduce impact.
- Exec ask: authorize a short-term burst of dedicated GPU headroom (+10 GPUs) for 4 hours to absorb the tail while we roll mitigations. This prevents customer-facing errors and buys time for a careful config rollout.
- Commercial ask: approve a 20% service credit for May for ClearBridge (retroactive to the start of this spike) contingent on a postmortem and a remediation plan from ClearBridge (they already paused the job).

Proposed immediate commitments (what we tell the customer now):
1) Status updates every 30 minutes until errors are back to baseline — OWNER: David (ops).
2) 4-hour burst authorization now (need Lauren/CTO ok) — OWNER: Infra (Marcus) once authorized.
3) Postmortem + tuning plan shared within 72 hours — OWNER: Product & SRE (Naomi / David).

If you can reply with a short approval phrase I can forward to infra and the customer: "Approved: +10 GPUs for 4 hours; 20% credit pending postmortem". If you want a different commercial number I can negotiate with ClearBridge but we should keep the mitigation timeline short.

Thanks — please advise fast, customer is watching.

Vivek
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
